subject.title: Feature: Dynamic header templating for custom LLM providers (enables Fireworks.ai prompt caching)

question: Should runtime request metadata remain provider-owned and typed, or should models.providers gain a generic placeholder language that can export session, agent, and run identifiers to arbitrary endpoints?
rationale: The alternatives create materially different core configuration, provider ownership, identifier-stability, and sensitive-metadata egress contracts, so implementation mechanics alone cannot safely choose the permanent direction.

options.title: Provider-Owned Typed Hooks
options.body: Use existing compatibility flags or provider plugin hooks with explicit opaque identifiers, adding generic API surface only for requirements those hooks cannot express.

options.title: Allowlisted Header Templates
options.body: Permit a small documented placeholder set with explicit endpoint trust, escaping, missing-value, precedence, compaction, and retry semantics.

options.title: Generic Request Templates
options.body: Create one template system spanning headers and request bodies and intentionally accept the larger security and compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Provider-Owned Typed Hooks
recommendation.body: Use existing compatibility flags or provider plugin hooks with explicit opaque identifiers, adding generic API surface only for requirements those hooks cannot express.
